title: §01-001: JavaScript Language Foundations & Environment
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §01-001 (JavaScript Language Foundations & Environment).

cards.concept: JavaScript Language Foundations & Environment: Execution Context Call Stack Lifecycle
cards.question: When a JavaScript function is invoked in the V8 engine, how is its Execution Context managed on the Call Stack?

options.text: It is allocated in libuv's threadpool and dispatched after epoll polling completes.
It is pushed onto the Call Stack with its LexicalEnvironment and VariableEnvironment records, and popped off upon function return.
It is serialized directly into bytecode cache and bypasses execution frames.
It remains permanently on the heap until cleared by Mark-Sweep garbage collection.

cards.explanation: V8 pushes a new Execution Context frame onto the Call Stack for every function invocation. When the function returns, its frame is popped in LIFO order.
cards.pitfall: Deep synchronous recursion exceeding stack limits triggers 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded'.
cards.citation: ECMAScript 2024 Specification §9.4 / MDN Web Docs: Call Stack

cards.concept: JavaScript Language Foundations & Environment: V8 Ignition Bytecode Interpreter
cards.question: What is the primary role of Ignition in Google's V8 JavaScript engine?

options.text: An optimizing compiler that compiles ASTs directly into unboxed x86 assembly.
A memory-efficient bytecode interpreter that generates bytecode from the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).
A generational garbage collector that compacts young generation semi-spaces.
An asynchronous event loop driver managing non-blocking socket descriptors.

cards.explanation: Ignition compiles ASTs into compact bytecode and executes it. As code runs, it collects type feedback; hot functions are subsequently compiled by TurboFan.
cards.codeSnippet:
// Inspection via V8 CLI flags:
// $ node --print-bytecode --print-bytecode-filter=calculate app.js
cards.pitfall: Writing polymorphic functions with fluctuating hidden classes forces TurboFan deoptimization back to Ignition bytecode.
cards.citation: V8 JavaScript Engine Documentation: Ignition Interpreter Architecture

cards.concept: JavaScript Language Foundations & Environment: ES Module vs Script Tag Loading
cards.question: How does script execution behavior differ when using `<script type="module">` compared to a standard `<script>` tag?

options.text: Module scripts execute synchronously immediately, blocking HTML parsing completely.
Module scripts are automatically deferred, executed in strict mode, and evaluated in isolated module scopes.
Module scripts share variables globally with standard inline script tags.
Module scripts can only be evaluated from local file:// URLs without CORS headers.

cards.explanation: ESM script tags are deferred by default (downloading in parallel and executing after HTML parse), enforce strict mode semantics, and prevent global variable pollution.
cards.codeSnippet:
<!-- Automatically deferred, strict mode, module scoped -->
<script type="module" src="app.js"></script>
cards.pitfall: Assuming top-level module variables attach to window/globalThis; ESM scopes are strictly isolated.
cards.citation: HTML Living Standard §4.12 / MDN Web Docs: JavaScript modules
